title: Short-term rental accommodation framework: code, register and Sydney 180-night cap (NSW)
summary: NSW introduced a Short-term Rental Accommodation Industry Code of Conduct (from 18 December 2020) and, from 1 November 2021, a mandatory premises register, fire safety standards and a 180-night cap on non-hosted stays in Greater Sydney.

instruments.title: Code of Conduct for the Short-term Rental Accommodation Industry

commenced.what: Premises register, planning framework and 180-night cap commenced

direction_rationale: Registration, night caps and levies raise costs or limit supply for short-term rental hosts, reducing competition faced by hotels and other accommodation providers.
comparison: States without STRA caps or registration before 2025 (QLD, SA); regional NSW (no cap) vs Greater Sydney
confounders: local council caps (e.g. Byron Shire 60 days)
price_series: Domestic holiday travel and accommodation; Rents
notes: Hosts are often not businesses in CABEE; listing data (e.g. Inside Airbnb) may be needed.

verified.notes: 18 Dec 2020 is from a law-firm note; 1 Nov 2021 is from Fair Trading's regulatory intent statement ('expected to commence') corroborated by a council page.

assessment.summary: A code of conduct, a mandatory register, fire safety rules and a 180-night cap on unhosted stays in Greater Sydney. It limits short-term rental supply and protects hotels from some competition; effects on long-term rental supply are not weighed here.

marks.reason: A 180-night cap on unhosted stays in Greater Sydney limits supply from hosts.
Hosts must register and meet fire safety and code requirements.
